newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia to split posts and telecoms - agency.
newsitem.headline: Croatia to split posts and telecoms - agency.

text.p: Croatian government drafted on Thursday a law which would split Croatian Posts and Telecommunications (HPT), thus paving the way for the sell-off of the telecoms business, Hina news agency said.

Transport Minister Zeljko Luzavac said the main thrust of the proposed law was the splitting of the two sectors of the HPT monopoly which already operate separately, a move that most European countries have already completed.

In recent a letter to the World Bank, the Croatian government committed itself to the privatisation of the large state-owned utilities, including HPT, energy, water and the roads sectors, and the oil monopoly INA by the end of 1999.
It said it would offer up to 30 percent of the attractive ones, including HPT, to foreign investors, possibly through flotations abroad.
With 354 million kuna after-tax profit in 1995 (figures for 1996 are not yet available), HPT is one of the most profitable Crotian companies.
Its total revenues in 1995 exceeded 3.8 billion kuna.
